perplexity.description:
Goodbye Jumbo is the second studio album by Welsh-British alternative rock band World Party, released in April 1990 on Ensign Records. The album showcases Karl Wallinger's ability to synthesize influences from his musical heroes into a cohesive alternative pop-rock sound. Recorded at Seaview Studios in London and The Old Rectory in Bedfordshire, the album spans 53 minutes across 12 tracks, blending college rock sensibilities with contemporary pop-rock arrangements.

The album achieved significant commercial and critical success. It peaked at No. 36 on the UK Albums Chart and No. 73 on the US Billboard 200, with strong international chart performance across Canada, Sweden, and Australia. The lead single "Way Down Now" dominated the US Billboard Alternative Songs chart, spending five weeks at number one, while follow-up single "Put the Message in the Box" reached No. 8 on the US modern rock chart. At year's end, Q Magazine named Goodbye Jumbo the best album of 1990, and it was voted the fifteenth best album of that year in The Village Voice's Pazz & Jop critics' poll. The album received a Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Music Performance at the 1991 ceremony and was later ranked 94th on Q's list of the "100 Greatest British Albums Ever" in 2000.
